get_exchange_volume.description: Read how much OKX itself traded in the last 24 hours, across everything it lists. One number for the size of the venue, for a market report or a week-on-week comparison. No API key required.
get_exchange_volume.name: get_exchange_volume

get_funding_rate.description: Read the next funding payment on a perpetual contract: the rate, when it settles, and which side pays, as a plain true/false rather than a sign you have to interpret. Funding is what keeps a perpetual near spot, so a persistently high rate is the market telling you it is crowded on one side. No API key required.
get_funding_rate.display_str_template: Get the OKX funding rate for {instrument}.
get_funding_rate.name: get_funding_rate

parameters.description: Which perpetual futures contract, e.g. BTC-USDT-SWAP. Funding is settled on perpetuals only, so no other market appears here.
parameters.name: instrument

as_of.description: When OKX generated this data, in UTC.

funding_rate.description: The predicted rate for the coming settlement.

funding_rate_percent.description: The same rate as a percentage.

instrument.description: The OKX instrument id, e.g. BTC-USDT.

interest_rate.description: The interest component of the funding formula.

longs_pay_shorts.description: True when longs pay shorts, false when shorts pay longs, so a workflow can read the direction without knowing the sign rule.

maximum_funding_rate.description: The ceiling OKX caps the rate at.

minimum_funding_rate.description: The floor OKX caps the rate at.

next_funding_rate.description: The rate forecast for the settlement after that.

next_funding_time.description: When that one settles, in UTC. The gap between the two is the funding interval, which OKX varies per contract.

premium.description: How far the contract is trading from the index, which is what drives the rate.

previous_funding_time.description: When funding last settled, in UTC.

settled_funding_rate.description: The rate that was actually charged last time.

settlement_state.description: settled, or processing while a settlement runs.

get_funding_rate_history.description: List what funding actually cost on a perpetual over a window, settlement by settlement, with the average across them. Use it to work out the real carrying cost of holding a position, which the current rate alone never shows. OKX keeps about three months. No API key required.
get_funding_rate_history.display_str_template: Get the OKX funding history for {instrument}.
get_funding_rate_history.name: get_funding_rate_history

parameters.description: Which perpetual futures contract, e.g. BTC-USDT-SWAP. Funding is settled on perpetuals only, so no other market appears here.
parameters.name: instrument

parameters.description: The earliest settlement to include. Leave it empty for the most recent ones. OKX keeps roughly three months of funding history.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: The latest settlement to include. Leave it empty to run up to now.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: The most settlements to return, newest first. Funding usually settles every eight hours, so 100 is about a month.
parameters.name: limit

average_rate.description: The mean realized rate across them.

average_rate_percent.description: The same average as a percentage.

funding_rate.description: The rate OKX predicted for the period.

funding_time.description: When this funding was settled, in UTC.

longs_paid_shorts.description: True when longs paid shorts, false when shorts paid longs, so a workflow can read the direction without knowing the sign rule.

realized_rate.description: The rate actually charged. This is the one that was paid.

realized_rate_percent.description: The realized rate as a percentage.

instrument.description: The OKX instrument id, e.g. BTC-USDT.

get_index_components.description: Show where an OKX index price comes from: which exchanges feed it, what each of them is quoting, and how much each one counts for. Use it to explain an index price, or to spot one venue drifting away from the rest. No API key required.
get_index_components.display_str_template: Get the sources behind the OKX {index} index.
get_index_components.name: get_index_components

index.description: The index that was read, e.g. BTC-USDT.

get_index_price.description: Read an OKX index: the reference price it computes from several exchanges rather than from its own order book, and the price its contracts settle against. Use it when you want the market's price for an asset rather than one venue's, and get the 24-hour move with it. No API key required.

get_mark_price.description: Read the mark price of a contract: the price OKX values open positions at, and the one liquidations are measured against. It is deliberately not the last traded price, so compare the two when a market looks stretched. No API key required.

get_open_interest.description: Read how much is open on a contract: the size of every position still outstanding, in contracts, in coins and in US dollars. Leave the contract empty for a whole derivatives market at once, ranked by size, with the total beside it. Rising open interest with a rising price means new money; falling means positions closing. No API key required.

get_order_book.description: Read the orders currently resting on both sides of an instrument, with the spread, the mid price and the volume stacked on each side already worked out. Use it to judge how much can be traded before the price moves. No API key required.

get_price_history.description: Get an instrument's price over time as candles: open, high, low, close and volume for each minute, hour, day, week or month, plus how it moved across the whole window in one summary. Leave the dates empty for the most recent candles, or pick a window years back: OKX splits recent and archived candles across two endpoints and this reads across both. No API key required.
get_price_history.display_str_template: Get the OKX price history of {instrument}.
get_price_history.name: get_price_history

parameters.description: Which OKX market the instrument trades on. It fills the instrument list below, and the step refuses an instrument that belongs to a different market, so a report meant to quote the spot price can never quietly quote a perpetual's instead.

parameters.description: The earliest point to include. Leave it empty to get the most recent candles instead of a window. Older ranges are served from OKX's archive automatically, so a date years back works the same as this morning.

description: Read live market data from OKX, one of the largest crypto exchanges: prices and 24-hour moves for any spot pair or futures contract, price history going back years, order books, recent trades, index prices and what they are built from, mark prices, perpetual funding rates and their history, open interest, the exchange's own trading volume, and whether OKX is in maintenance. Everything here is public market data: no account, no API key, and no access to anyone's balances or orders.
